announcements.text: vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe.
announcements.evidence: Intake n=265/n=267: the file carries nine copies of one fleet-root key, committed and pushed, and byte-identical to the file the live gatus container mounts. Three re-exposures in 48 h by two lanes while working on that file: n=275 (grep -A8) and n=285 (json.dumps of a parsed endpoint dict). Remedy pending and owner-gated: render the config at deploy time so no key lives in a readable file.

announcements.text: Pacemaker cron triggers on this box still pass --mode quiet for three jobs, NONE of them meta-factory's: ai-antispam-owner-digest and ai-antispam-triage-sweep (ai-antispam), and oc-triage-owner-digest (opencrabs-dev) — all three enabled. The owner re-ruling of 2026-09-19T03:34:30Z / 03:36:54Z made turn-end THE default for all lane traffic and retained quiet only for batch/fan-out notices whose ack contract is the ledger; a single-lane pacemaker is not batch/fan-out, so each of these defers instead of waking an idle lane immediately. Meta-factory's four were moved to explicit --mode turn-end on 2026-09-23 (byte-verified; schedule and next_run_at preserved). CAUTION FOR WHOEVER FIXES THE REMAINING THREE — the cap flag cannot be dropped alone: each carried --mode quiet --quiet-for-secs 20 --max-delay-secs 30, and its prompt documented WHY the cap was there, namely that quiet's DEFAULT starvation cap of 1800s blocks past the tool's 120s budget and kills the trigger. That hazard is quiet-specific and vanishes under turn-end, so the mode and the cap move TOGETHER and the sentence justifying the cap must be rewritten with them, or the prompt ends up arguing for a flag it no longer carries. Read live 2026-09-23T11:31Z: of 55 cron rows, 13 carry --mode — 10 turn-end, 3 quiet.
announcements.evidence: cron_jobs read via mode=ro URI at 2026-09-19T14:21Z: --mode values across all 36 cron prompts = {quiet: 8}; zero use the retired now. Meta-factory's five: factory-measurement-daily, factory-triage-patrol, factory-insights-weekly, factory-template-weekly, factory-growth-map-biweekly.

announcements.text: A cron job whose run is interrupted by an OpenCrabs daemon restart delivers its result to NO channel: boot revival resumes the turn with no job identity, run id or deliver_to, so the job output reaches nobody. Ship-chain hot-reloads make restarts frequent, so any factory relying on cron delivery is exposed.
announcements.evidence: Root-caused by Infra Factory HQ and filed upstream as leshchenko1979/opencrabs#382 (OPEN, filed 2026-09-19T06:47:53Z). Two independent jobs confirmed in the daemon log: infra-sender-logs-check - 186 span lines before the 2026-09-18 15:09:34 restart, 0 after; infra-surveys-daily - 792 before the 2026-09-19 06:08:33 restart, 0 after. Ruling doc: /root/vds-servers/docs/rulings/2026-09-19-cron-result-lost-on-restart.md

announcements.text: session_notify's 'now' mode is RETIRED and passing it FAILS the delivery outright - it is not merely discouraged. 'turn-end' is the default and wakes an idle target immediately, so it loses nothing 'now' ever delivered; 'quiet' is retained for batch notices whose ack contract is the ledger. 'interrupt' is the URGENT tier (#393): it delivers at the SAME boundary as turn-end and adds precedence framing so the target yields its current plan and answers in that turn - never deferred, never a default, spell it explicitly. It is NOT pre-emption: no boundary exists inside a running tool call, so a mid-turn target still queues for its next tool-loop boundary. Legacy interrupt:true UPGRADES a non-quiet resolution to that tier. A 'no wake observed' confirm verdict means the target is mid-turn; never re-send on it.
announcements.evidence: fork issues #373 ('now' retired) and #393 (interrupt = urgent tier); notify_policy.rs returns Err for mode=now and resolves interrupt=true to DeliveryMode::Interrupt; the delivery.mode enum is exactly [turn-end, interrupt, quiet] at notify.rs:171. Code leg 07b6372c4, 2026-09-20T22:20:22Z, ancestor of the deployed sha.

announcements.text: Brain metrics are a STANDING reading with an instrument: tools/brain_metrics.py (no args needed; --home / --hours / --log-dir) prints all three legs with their predicate, population and instant, and gates none of them. The clause that binds it is docs/measurement-procedure.md section 5; its gate is tests/test_brain_metrics.py. A figure in this notice is a DATED READING and never current — run the instrument. Read 2026-09-23T11:28:08Z: LEG A, the always-injected Tier 0 triple (SOUL.md, USER.md, AGENTS.md, named in docs/methodology/04-harness-binding.md; these live in NO repository, so a leg-A reading has an INSTANT for its identity and no revision) 698 lines / 133877 bytes / about 38250 tokens = 19.12 percent of a 200k window — AGENTS.md alone is 641 lines / 129188 bytes, 91.83 percent of injected lines. LEG B, every skills/*/SKILL.md at depth 1, 755 lines / 74467 bytes / about 21276 tokens = 10.64 percent; skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md alone is 755 lines, 255 over the owner's 500-line budget marker (the marker is PRINTED, never gated). TOGETHER 1453 lines / 208344 bytes / about 59526 tokens = 29.76 percent of the window, paid before a session reads its first message. The previous read in this notice (2026-09-21T22:48:40Z: 1337 / 171399 / 24.48 percent) is kept as the step this one follows, never overwritten: the floor rose 5.28 points in about 1.7 days and AGENTS.md is most of it. LEG C IS CURRENTLY UNREADABLE, and this notice therefore carries NO leg-C figure. Its needle is the summarizer line 'Compaction: sending N / N messages to summarizer (X / Y input tokens, reserving Z for output)' at src/brain/agent/service/context.rs:1084. Measured 2026-09-23: that needle occurs 28 to 2330 times per day across the ops logs of 09-16 through 09-21, and ZERO times in the 09-22 and 09-23 logs — the population collapsed at that boundary and has not returned. The emitting call is tracing::info! and the configured level is info, and the string is present in the running binary (v0.5.3), so this is NOT a logging-level change; the cause is not yet established, and both a superseded compaction path and an emission regression fit. The instrument handles it correctly: it prints 'no event in this window this run' and exits 4 rather than returning a silent zero. Treat any leg-C figure dated before 2026-09-22 as un-refreshable from this surface. CAUTION: the trigger line 'Context at NN percent' at compaction.rs uses a DIFFERENT denominator (effective tokens over effective max, i.e. the window minus reserves) and must never be read as a fraction of the provider window.

announcements.text: session_notify's 'now' mode is RETIRED and passing it FAILS the delivery outright - it is not merely discouraged. 'turn-end' is the default and wakes an idle target immediately, so it loses nothing 'now' ever delivered; 'quiet' is retained for batch notices whose ack contract is the ledger. 'interrupt' is the URGENT tier (#393): it delivers at the SAME boundary as turn-end and adds precedence framing so the target yields its current plan and answers in that turn - never deferred, never a default, spell it explicitly. It is NOT pre-emption: no boundary exists inside a running tool call, so a mid-turn target still queues for its next tool-loop boundary. Legacy interrupt:true UPGRADES a non-quiet resolution to that tier. A 'no wake observed' confirm verdict means the target is mid-turn; never re-send on it.
announcements.evidence: fork issues #373 ('now' retired) and #393 (interrupt = urgent tier); notify_policy.rs returns Err for mode=now and resolves interrupt=true to DeliveryMode::Interrupt; the delivery.mode enum is exactly [turn-end, interrupt, quiet] at notify.rs:171.
